history.summary: AMBIGUITY: Junagadh has two major Swaminarayan temples — the 1828 original on Jawahar Road (also called Shri Radha Ramana Temple, documented here) and a newer BAPS temple at Akshar Wadi on the Somnath road built under Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The CSV's generic 'Swaminarayan Temple' is mapped to the older, historically documented one. Ordered built by Swaminarayan himself, founder of the Swaminarayan Sampraday. The land was gifted by King Hemantsinh (Jinabhai, Darbar of Panchala); the foundation stone was laid by Gunatitanand Swami on 10 May 1826 (construction supervised by Brahmanand Swami); on 1 May 1828 Swaminarayan personally installed Shri Ranchhodrai and Trikamrai in the inner sanctum, Radharaman Dev and Harikrishna Maharaj in the east, and Siddheswar Mahadev, Parvati, Ganesha and Nandishwar in the west. Gunatitanand Swami served as first mahant for 40+ years; the Mughal Subba Bahadur Khan visited during the installation. The temple has five spires and a 278-ft circumference. Coordinates (21.5222, 70.4579) are APPROXIMATE: Junagadh town centre, as no published POI-level coordinates for the Jawahar Road temple were found.

name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Junagadh
town_description: Junagadh is a historic city in Gujarat's Saurashtra region, nestled at the foot of Mount Girnar. Its past stretches from Ashoka's 3rd-century BCE rock edicts and the Uparkot Fort to the Nawabi-era Mahabat Maqbara, and it is a major pilgrimage hub for both Hindus and Jains.

travel.airport: Keshod (~40 km) or Rajkot (~103 km) from Junagadh
travel.railway: Junagadh Junction (~4 km from the temple, per Trawell)
travel.road: Located on Jawahar Road, Dipanjali locality, in the centre of Junagadh town
